record.original_question: Let (Omega, mu) be a sigma-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L2(Omega), let a: V x V -> C be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, let -A generate the associated bounded analytic semigroup (T(t)) on L2(Omega), and assume that (T(t)) is L-infinity-bounded in the sense that there exists M >= 1 with ||T(t)f||_infinity <= M ||f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega). Must there exist a function g in L-infinity(Omega) with g > 0 mu-almost everywhere and 1/g in L-infinity(Omega) such that ||g T(t)f||_infinity <= ||g f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega) and all t >= 0?

evidence.quote: The semigroup (T (t))t≥0 is called L∞ -bounded, if there exists M > 0 such that kT (t)f k∞ ≤ Mkf k∞ , for all f ∈ L2 (Ω) ∩ L∞ (Ω).
It is clear that (T (t))t≥0 is L∞ -bounded if there exists a function g ∈ L∞ (Ω) with g > 0 µ-a.e. and 1/g ∈ L∞ (Ω) satisfying kgT (t)f k∞ ≤ kgf k∞ for all f ∈ L∞ (Ω) ∩ L2 (Ω).

Problem 22 (L∞ -contraction for a weight problem). In the setting of Problem 21 assume that the semigroup (T (t))t≥0 is L∞ -bounded, i.e., satisfies (1) for some M ≥ 1. Does there exist a function g ∈ L∞ (Ω) satisfying g > 0 µ-a.e., 1/g ∈ L∞ (Ω), and (3)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space and let $V$ be a dense linear subspace of $L^2(\Omega)$. Let $a:V\times V\to\mathbb{C}$ be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, and let $-A$ be the associated operator on $L^2(\Omega)$, which generates a bounded analytic semigroup $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ on $L^2(\Omega)$.

Assume that $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ is $L^\infty$-bounded, meaning that there exists a constant $M\ge 1$ such that
$$\|T(t)f\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \le M\,\|f\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \qquad \text{for all } f\in L^2(\Omega)\cap L^\infty(\Omega) \text{ and all } t\ge 0.$$

Question: Must there exist a measurable function $g:\Omega\to(0,\infty)$ with $g\in L^\infty(\Omega)$, $g>0$ $\mu$-almost everywhere, and $1/g\in L^\infty(\Omega)$, such that
$$\|g\,T(t)f\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \le \|g\,f\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \qquad \text{for all } f\in L^2(\Omega)\cap L^\infty(\Omega) \text{ and all } t\ge 0\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent collection of open problems on sesquilinear forms and operator semigroups. A web search did not reveal a published resolution (positive or negative) of the weighted $L^\infty$-contraction question; related literature characterizes $L^\infty$-contractivity via form conditions but does not appear to address the weighted reduction asked here.

status_evidence.snippet: Problem 22 (L∞-contraction for a weight problem): assuming the semigroup is L∞-bounded, does there exist a weight g with g, 1/g ∈ L∞ such that gT(t) is L∞-contractive?
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Sesquilinear Forms and Analytic Semigroups (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses characterizations of L∞-contractivity via form conditions for analytic semigroups generated by sectorial forms.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature characterizes L∞-contractivity but not the weighted reduction asked.
